topic.title: Why is the east side of England's old cities the poorer side?
topic.map_answer: the prevailing wind's direction across a city map: westerly winds carried factory smoke to the east side, so the rich settled upwind in the west and the poor were left downwind in the east

title: Why are English cities poorer in the east?
description:
Why is the east side of so many old English cities the poorer side?
England's industrial cities, the wind that blows across them, and the factory smoke it carried east, on the map.
Sources: Heblich, Trew and Zylberberg, Journal of Political Economy (May 2021). The characters are not advisers.
Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
